 Austin weather: Sunday rain and flood risk
 By Leslie London FOX Local Weather Published  November 8, 2026 8:23 AM CST Share
 Copy Link 
 Email 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Reddit 
 Published  November 8, 2026 8:23 AM CST Austin weather: Nov. 8 evening forecast 
 FOX 7's Cary Burgess gives the latest weather forecast for all of Central Texas.
 The Brief
 Widespread rain and cooler weather are impacting Central Texas, with heavier storms and flash flood threats concentrated farther south. 
 Temperatures will stay unseasonably cool near 62 degrees Sunday, with light, scattered showers lingering into Monday. 
 Drier, sunnier conditions and warmer highs in the 70s are forecast to return starting Tuesday and continue through the week. 
 AUSTIN - Continuous rainfall, cool temperatures, and the potential for localized flash flooding marked the start of the weekend across Central Texas, with heavier storms striking areas further south.
 Continuous rainfall
 A broad weather system is bringing widespread showers and occasional thunderstorms to the Austin area. While the heaviest precipitation and active flash flood warnings remain concentrated in southern Texas, rain continues to track across the entire Central Texas viewing area.
 Rainfall began moving into the Hill Country on Saturday afternoon before becoming more widespread overnight. Mason and Gillespie counties, along with areas around Fredericksburg, experienced some of the heaviest early rain, with parts of San Saba County recording more than an inch of precipitation over 24 hours.
 Although rainfall is expected to taper off gradually Sunday evening, residents should carry rain gear and stay alert for potential weather warnings, particularly in low-lying or flood-prone locations west and south of Austin.
 Cloud cover and persistent moisture will keep Sunday's temperatures unseasonably cool. Daytime highs are projected to reach around 62 degrees, only a slight increase from morning temperatures in the upper 50s, which included 59 degrees in Bastrop and San Marcos and 58 degrees in Rockdale and Williamson County. Dew points are expected to remain in the upper 50s, keeping humidity levels comfortable.
 Monday weather
 Unsettled weather will linger into Monday with additional light, scattered showers anticipated, though totals are expected to remain manageable around 1 inch.
 Conditions will clear significantly as the workweek progresses. Rain chances decrease sharply after Monday, allowing sunshine to return alongside warmer afternoon temperatures in the 70s through the remainder of the week.
